### 2026-10-11 – What I wanted to do

**2h**

What I wanted to do

Continue Starbie's firmware, although I barely have time because of exams.
Why: I'm motivated to learn hardware and I don't want to miss the opportunity to win the 3D printer.

Problem 1: Arduino IDE on Wayland

I followed the guide; the first step was to install the IDE.
I discovered that it has many issues with Wayland and doesn't run properly.
I paused the recording to try to fix it.
It didn't get fixed and I didn't want to keep wasting time, so I switched to Windows to save myself the trouble.

Problem 2: Compilation error on Windows

On Windows I was able to follow the steps in the guide.
When compiling I had a couple of errors which I solved off-camera with help from Gemini.
It was something related to Windows Smart App Control (according to Gemini, "apparently").riscv32-esp-elf-g++: fatal error: cannot execute 'C:/Users/simon/AppData/Local/Arduino15/packages/esp32/tools/esp-rv32/2601/bin/../libexec/gcc/riscv32-esp-elf/14.2.0/cc1plus.exe': CreateProcess: No such file or directory

compilation terminated.

exit status 1

Compilation error: exit status 1
It took me a good while.

Now I'm changing the sprite with help from Claude. I changed the arrays code section by the bee sprite

 How I feel about the result

I'm not very satisfied, but I think I did well: it's my first time doing something like this.

 What's next

After exams I plan to redesign it.
Change the hexagon design to a more elaborate one following the bee theme, in honor of my fursona.
